source.title: One-layer transformers fail to solve the induction heads task
source.authors: C. Sanford; Daniel Hsu; Matus Telgarsky

record.tranche_reason: It gives a theoretical lower bound for solving the induction heads task with a one-layer transformer, using a communication-complexity argument rather than the original empirical method.
record.gate_note: The two-layer construction is cited from prior work, not tested here. The paper does not measure training dynamics, in-context learning, or the internal composition of attention heads.
record.test_reason: The paper proves that a one-layer transformer needs size hmp = Ω(n) to solve the 1-hop induction heads task. This formalises V1's premise that the [A][B]…[A]→[B] behaviour needs cross-layer composition in small models. It is a theoretical capacity result: it measures no trained heads, training dynamics or in-context learning.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors prove that any one-layer transformer solving the 1-hop induction heads task over a three-symbol alphabet needs hmp = Ω(n). This is exponentially larger than the size sufficient for two-layer transformers, per cited constructions (Bietti et al. 2023; Sanford et al. 2024).
record.recipe_differences: A theoretical communication-complexity lower-bound proof for a formal task, rather than an empirical study of head formation or training dynamics.
record.problems: The result is a theorem for a formal transformer model, not an empirical measurement of learned heads or training. The two-layer comparison is cited from prior work rather than tested in this paper.

untested.parts: Whether trained models actually form induction heads by composing with a previous-token head. Whether two-layer models use that mechanism. Whether the result holds in attention-only models specifically: the formal model has no MLP, but this is not studied empirically.
All: training-time formation, abruptness, in-context learning gain, loss bump.
All: role in in-context learning of large models.
All: presence across families, sizes, runs and modalities.
All: dependence on data or training setup.
All: mechanisms of few-shot task learning.

record.verdict_notes: A short theoretical note using a reduction from the INDEX communication problem. The bound also implies that a large enough one-layer model can in principle solve the task, so 'cannot' is size-relative. The support for V1 concerns only depth necessity, not the specific previous-token-head composition circuit in trained models.

versions.untested_parts: The paper tests the formal induction heads task and one-layer capacity, but not whether heads form by composing with a previous-token head or whether a two-layer model uses that mechanism.
